indicator_definition: This indicator measures gross domestic expenditure on research and development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP. R&D expenditure covers all creative and systematic work to increase knowledge and devise new applications. It is a key indicator for monitoring innovation intensity. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national R&D surveys.
rationale: Investment in R&D is a key driver of innovation, competitiveness and long-term productivity growth. Increasing R&D expenditure helps develop new technologies, improve processes and create high-quality jobs. Progress means a sustained increase in R&D expenditure as a share of GDP.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through national R&D surveys following the OECD Frascati Manual. GERD covers all R&D performed on national territory regardless of funding source, including basic research, applied research and experimental development. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
indicator_name: Research and development expenditure as share of GDP
